newsitem.title: CHINA: Hewlett-Packard sees China sales up 50 percent.
newsitem.headline: Hewlett-Packard sees China sales up 50 percent.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co. expects revenues in China to soar more than 50 percent in 1997 from a total of $550 million last year, company officials said Monday.
"China has been strategically elevated as the major investment market for Hewlett-Packard," Hewlett-Packard Vice President Alex Sozonoff told a news briefing.

Computer products, which accounted for $330 million of China revenues in 1996, would continue to dominate sales this year, said Sun Cheng-Yaw, general manager of China Hewlett-Packard Co.'s Computer Systems Organisation.
Hewlett-Packard has invested more than $200 million in China over the past 18 months and is considering a number of new projects, he said, but gave no details.

China Hewlett-Packard, a joint venture with the China Electronic Import and Export Corp., had a 6.5 percent share of the Chinese computer market and was China's largest PC server supplier, company officials said.
The U.S. firm was ploughing funds into infrastructure and staff but expected to see returns on its investments in about three years, Sozonoff said but gave no details.
